item.title: Open Informatics part three: down to the metal
item.description: The hardware side of Open Informatics at CTU Prague, taken from the actual lab sheets. The RISC-V based Computer Architectures course every student takes, the faculty-built MZ_APO board and its two-player Snake semester project, then the Internet of Things chain: electromagnetism, FPGA design in VHDL, real network equipment, ARM microcontrollers, and a steer-by-wire capstone on a real-time operating system.

item.title: Open Informatics part two: the minor specialisations
item.description: The flexibility half of the Open Informatics bachelor at CTU Prague. How minors work (three courses, no registration, printed on your diploma), all seven in-house minors from Artificial Intelligence to Mathematics, and the inter-university prg.ai Minor that spans four faculties at two universities.

item.title: Open Informatics in Prague: the four bachelor areas, and FEL vs FIT
item.description: A deep dive into the Open Informatics bachelor at CTU Prague's Faculty of Electrical Engineering: the maths-heavy shared core, and all four specialisations - AI and Computer Science, Software, Internet of Things, and Computer Games and Graphics. Plus how informatics at the electrical engineering faculty differs from the Faculty of Information Technology.

item.title: Beslutningsvegring: når friheten blir en forbannelse (norsk)
item.description: Norsk versjon. To verter tar for seg artikkelen der professor Paul Otto Brunstad kaller beslutningsvegring en folkesykdom: valgfrihetens paradoks, det psykologiske immunforsvaret, pre-mortem, gartnerbildet, og hvorfor det aldri er trygt a sitte stille i baten.

item.title: Decision Paralysis: When Freedom Becomes a Curse
item.description: Two hosts unpack a Norwegian article where a professor calls decision avoidance a public health problem. The paradox of choice, the psychological immune system, pre-mortems, and why sitting still in the boat is not a neutral position.

item.title: LetterTranscriber: reading 1930s handwriting with AI (preview)
item.description: A two-minute preview: how a Flask app turns scanned Norwegian letters from the 1920s and 30s into corrected, annotated transcripts using Gemini.
